title: 2025: The year in LLMs
summary: Willison's third annual review of the LLM year, 26 sections. Key themes: coding agents crossing from 'mostly works' to 'actually works' in November 2025, all major labs releasing CLI coding agents, introduction of reasoning models trained on code with RL. His own hand-written code dropped to single-digit percentage of output.

title: The last six months in LLMs, illustrated by pelicans on bicycles
summary: Annotated keynote transcript from AI Engineer World's Fair 2025. Won best-of-conference. Willison had to cut scope from 'the past year' to 'the past six months' due to accelerating pace. Covers Claude Code launch, coding agents, multimodal advances.

title: A new way to extract detailed transcripts from Claude Code
summary: Announces claude-code-transcripts Python CLI tool. Converts JSONL session files and Claude Code for web exports into multi-page HTML. Supports --gist option to auto-publish to GitHub Gist with shareable preview URL. Practical tool for sharing Claude Code sessions publicly.

title: Agentic Engineering Patterns
summary: Willison's three core agentic engineering patterns: (1) red/green TDD loop, (2) templates for repeated task shapes, (3) hoarding — accumulating context artifacts across sessions. Coined 'agentic engineering' as the discipline of working effectively with LLM agents.

title: My LLM coding workflow going into 2026
summary: Widely-cited workflow guide. Core principles: treat LLM as powerful pair programmer requiring clear direction; break work into iterative tickets not monolithic outputs; import full GitHub repo into Claude Projects for context; review everything the AI suggests. Anthropic engineers write ~90% of Claude Code's own code using Claude Code.

title: The Code Agent Orchestra — what makes multi-agent coding work
summary: Covers orchestrating multiple AI agents across codebases. Discusses Claude Code's Agent Teams for true parallel execution with shared task lists and dependency tracking. Three orchestration tiers: interactive (single session), sprint (parallel worktrees), overnight backlog drain.

title: The future of agentic coding: conductors to orchestrators
summary: Evolution from developer-as-conductor (directing single agents) to developer-as-orchestrator (managing agent swarms). Also published on O'Reilly Radar. Covers when multi-agent is justified vs single-agent, and the shift in developer role.

title: How we use Claude Code today at Intercom
summary: Practical field notes from Intercom's all-in Claude Code adoption. 13 plugins, 100+ skills, production-safe hooks (read-replica only, blocked critical tables, Okta auth, DynamoDB audit trail). Telemetry infrastructure for measuring AI adoption. 95%+ of daily code now AI-generated.

title: Why Garry Tan's Claude Code setup has gotten so much love, and hate
summary: TechCrunch coverage of gstack going viral after Tan's March 12 2026 tweet. 20k+ stars, 2200+ forks. Critics argue similar prompt sets existed privately, that YC CEO prominence gave undue attention, and some productivity claims (37k LOC/day) were exaggerated. Pro side: concrete productivity evidence with 60-day metrics.

title: LLM Wiki pattern (GitHub Gist)
summary: Karpathy's gist describing a three-layer LLM-maintained knowledge base: raw/ (immutable sources), wiki/ (LLM-maintained markdown with cross-references), schema/ (config directing agent behavior). Compiler analogy: raw = source code, LLM = compiler, wiki = executable. Hit 27,900 stars; spawned dozens of open-source implementations.

title: AI Tooling for Software Engineers in 2026
summary: Pragmatic Engineer survey (Jan 27 - Feb 17 2026, ~1000 respondents). Key findings: 95% use AI tools weekly or more; 75% use AI for 50%+ of SE work; Claude Code nearly as widespread as GitHub Copilot was in 2023; Cursor growing 35% since previous survey; 55% regularly use AI agents; staff+ engineers heaviest agent users at 63.5%; OpenAI Codex already at 60% of Cursor usage despite not existing in last survey; 70% use 2-4 tools simultaneously.

title: Claude Code and the Art of Test-Driven Development
summary: TDD serves a critical function in AI-assisted development: keeps the developer in the loop when directing thousands of lines of code generation. Tests are the forcing function that prevents blindly adopting AI output. When using Claude with TDD, being explicit about TDD prevents Claude from creating mock implementations prematurely.

title: Why Does Test-Driven Development Work So Well In 'AI'-assisted Programming?
summary: Practitioner analysis of why TDD pairs naturally with AI coding. Work one feature at a time, solve one problem at a time, run tests at every step. Red/green/refactor provides built-in success conditions that both the developer and AI can verify.

title: LLM predictions for 2026, shared with Oxide and Friends
summary: Willison's 1, 3, and 6 year predictions for AI/LLM industry. LLM code quality becomes undeniable in 2026. Predicts 'dark factory' pattern where AI does its own QA without human review. Also available as Oxide and Friends podcast episode.

title: The Tiny Teams Playbook
summary: swyx's patterns for small AI-native teams doing the work of much larger traditional teams. Covers how coding agents change team structure, when to use multi-agent, and the new economics of software development.

title: Claude Code: Anthropic's Agent in Your Terminal
summary: Latent Space deep-dive on Claude Code at/near launch. Features Cat Wu and Boris Cherny from Anthropic discussing the tool's design, use cases, and workflow integration.
